meta.title: QualiPulse · AI voice interviews, decision-ready insights
meta.description: QualiPulse runs AI-moderated voice interviews with your users and turns them into a decision-ready research memo. Themes, verbatim quotes and recommendations in hours, not weeks. 3 free interviews, no credit card.

hero.title: The customer interviews you keep postponing. Done by Friday.
hero.sub: QualiPulse interviews your users by voice, right in their browser, asking adaptive follow-ups like a trained researcher. You get transcripts, themes, and a decision memo where every claim traces back to a verbatim quote. No scheduling. No moderating. No transcription weekend.

live.q1: You mentioned you almost cancelled back in March. Walk me through what happened that week.
live.a1: Honestly? The price went up, I looked at my statement, and I thought: do I even use this anymore…
live.q2: You said “do I even use this.” What would using it look like on a good week?
live.a2: Good question. Probably the Monday planning thing. When I skip that, the whole subscription feels pointless.

strip.audience: Built for product teams, UX researchers, agencies and anyone who listens to the voice of the customer

problem.title: Nobody skips research because they don’t care. They skip it because it’s slow.
problem.subtitle: By the time a classic interview study is scheduled, moderated, transcribed and synthesised, the decision it was meant to inform has already shipped.

cards.title: Calendar tetris
cards.desc: Recruiting, timezone juggling, no-shows, reschedules. Eight interviews means three weeks of logistics before you’ve learned a single thing.

cards.title: Per interview, all-in
cards.desc: Moderate it, transcribe it, code it, synthesise it. Multiply by every participant. That cost is exactly why “let’s just A/B it” wins the meeting.

cards.title: Insight after the decision
cards.desc: Findings that arrive after the roadmap is locked don’t change anything. They become a slide nobody reopens.

problem.kicker: So teams decide on gut feel, a survey with 4% completion, and the loudest customer in the Slack channel, then call it “being scrappy.”

how.title: Brief it tonight. Read the memo by Friday.
how.subtitle: QualiPulse collapses the whole pipeline into three steps: recruiting logistics, moderating, transcription, and synthesis.

steps.title: Describe the decision
steps.desc: Tell the research copilot what you need to decide. It drafts an interview guide with sections, screening questions and follow-up intents. You edit anything.

steps.title: Share one link
steps.desc: Participants open it in any browser and just talk. The AI listens, probes the interesting bits, and keeps to your time budget. No app, no booking, no moderator.

steps.title: Read the decision memo
steps.desc: Themes, tensions, jobs-to-be-done and recommendations, each backed by verbatim quotes you can walk back to the exact second.

evidence.title: Every claim is walk-back-able.
evidence.subtitle: AI summaries are only useful if you can check them. Click a finding, and QualiPulse shows you the verbatim quote, the participant, and the timestamp it came from. Try it:

claims.title: Cancellation is a billing-moment event
claims.sub: 9 of 12 participants located the decision at a statement, renewal email, or price change, not at a moment of product frustration.
claims.quote: “I wasn’t even annoyed at the product. <m>The renewal email landed and I just thought, that’s €29 I didn’t decide to spend.</m> That was the whole thing.”

claims.title: “Pause” is the unbuilt feature they wanted
claims.sub: Participants didn’t want to leave. They wanted to stop paying during low-usage months without losing history.
claims.quote: “<m>If I could have frozen it for the summer I’d still be a customer.</m> Instead the options were pay or delete, so… I deleted.”

claims.title: Losing history is the real switching cost
claims.sub: Fear of losing past work kept several participants subscribed months after they stopped using the product weekly.
claims.quote: “Honestly the only reason I’m still paying is <m>three years of notes are in there and I don’t trust the export</m>. That’s not loyalty, that’s hostage-keeping.”

evidence.note: This traceability runs through the whole product: tag quotes into your own codebook, annotate themes as confirmed or disputed, and re-run the analysis with your notes folded in. The AI drafts; you stay the researcher.

items.title: Adaptive follow-ups
items.desc: The AI decides after every answer: probe deeper, move on, or wrap up. It paces itself against your time budget, like a moderator watching the clock.

items.title: People say more than they type
items.desc: A spoken answer runs four to six times longer than a text-box answer, with the hedges and half-thoughts where the real insight hides.

items.title: Screening built in
items.desc: Disqualifying questions run before the interview starts, so you never pay for a participant who wasn’t your audience.

items.title: Quality scoring per interview
items.desc: Each transcript gets an AI quality assessment, so thin or off-topic sessions are flagged before they pollute your synthesis.

items.title: Your codebook, your calls
items.desc: Tag quotes, write memos, dispute themes. Refined analyses fold in your annotations. Iterative, not one-shot.

items.title: Cross-study decision memos
items.desc: Synthesise up to 8 studies into one executive memo, with conflicts surfaced, not smoothed over.

faq.title: The things people ask before their first study.

items.question: What exactly costs a credit?
items.answer: Only a completed interview of up to 15 minutes. Participants who are screened out, abandon halfway, or hit a technical failure never consume a credit. That risk is ours, not yours.

items.question: Do participants need to install anything?
items.answer: No. They open your link in any browser (phone or laptop), pass a 10-second mic check, and talk. Consent, screening and resume-where-you-left-off are all built into the flow.

items.question: Do I need to recruit participants?
items.answer: QualiPulse gives you shareable links for your own participants: customers, users, a mailing list, an in-product prompt. You stay in control of who you interview.

items.question: Is an AI interviewer as good as a human moderator?
items.answer: For discovery and evaluative research, it’s remarkably close. It never leads the witness, never gets tired on interview #9, and asks follow-ups grounded in what the participant just said. For deeply sensitive topics, we’d still recommend a human. The honest pitch: an AI-moderated interview beats the survey you were going to send instead.

items.question: How do I know the analysis isn’t hallucinated?
items.answer: Every theme, tension and recommendation carries verbatim quotes that link to the exact transcript turn. Click through and read the source. You can mark themes confirmed, disputed or needs-evidence, and the refined analysis has to answer to your annotations.

items.question: What languages are supported?
items.answer: Interviews run in the language of your study. English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Italian are available today, and we add more regularly. The researcher workspace is available in English and French, and any transcript can be machine-translated as a reading aid, with the original always kept as the source of truth.

items.question: Who owns the research data?
items.answer: You do. Recordings, transcripts and reports belong to your workspace, databases live in the EU, audio is encrypted at rest, and we never train AI models on your research. GDPR-aligned processing with a signed DPA, subprocessor list and participant notice available.
